validated_results.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet and risk of bladder cancer in the EPIC cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective EPIC cohort analysis reports the association between adherence to the Mediterranean diet and incident urothelial cell bladder cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: High versus low relative Mediterranean diet score (rMED)
extraction.population: EPIC cohort participants recruited between 1991 and 2000

sample_size.excerpt: The analysis included 477,312 participants, recruited from ten European countries between 1991 and 2000.

cases.excerpt: During an average follow-up of 11 years, 1,425 participants (70.9% male) were diagnosed with a first primary UCC.

effect_size.excerpt: There was a negative but non-significant association between a high versus low rMED score and risk of UCC overall (HR: 0.84 [95% CI 0.69, 1.03]) and risk of aggressive (HR: 0.88 [95% CI 0.61, 1.28]) and non-aggressive tumors (HR: 0.78 [95% CI 0.54, 1.14]).
